the multipolar regionalization is a better model than the unipolar one for describing the world cities' networks of multinational firms, and that the FTZs and continental regions are good proxies of the multipolar classes.
the network of world regions is multipolar and the most cohesive regions are located in North America, East Asia and Western Europe.
the network of world city connections, as represented by multinational corporations, is organized in four classes, each with a different degree of cohesion.

the identification of the most cohesive sub‐networks of the global network of world cities.
the multipolar regionalization, which is not only a theoretical question, but also a practical one, since it has implications for the design of FTZs and the development of the world economy.
the multipolarization of the network of cities in the world.

the network of multinational corporations is not a simple centre–periphery system, but rather a complex multipolar one.
the network of cities is more complex and dynamic than previously thought.
cities' roles and functions are not static, but rather dynamic and changing, depending on the industry or service, and the multinational groups' strategies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multipolar regions of world cities are not necessarily the FTZs, and that the multinational firms' networks are a powerful tool to understand the global economy.
the world city network is more multipolar than the world trade network and that the multipolar regionalization is more visible in the services than in the industries, with a few exceptions.
the network of multinational firms' subsidiaries in the 503 cities is organized around a multipolar structure, which is more complex and less hierarchical than the unipolar model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the network of cities, as a proxy for the global economy, is not a unipolar system but rather a multipolar system, which can be used as a benchmark for the analysis of the global economy.
the multipolar regionalization, which is a new way of thinking, is more appropriate for the analysis of the global network of cities than the centre–periphery approach.
a new regionalization of cities is emerging in multinational firms' global networks, and that this new regionalization is not necessarily linked to traditional regionalization patterns.
